question: A and B complete a work in 14 days. If A alone can do it in 56 days, then B alone can do three-fourth of the same work in days.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Combined efficiency (A+B) = Total Work ÷ Days = 56 ÷ 14 = 4

A efficiency = 56 ÷ 56 = 1

B efficiency = 4 − 1 = 3

Time for B to do 3/4 work = (3/4 × 56) ÷ 3 = 42 ÷ 3 = 14 days

**∴ The correct answer is 14 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Time taken by (A+B) = 14 days, Time taken by A = 56 days.

**Formula:** 1/B = 1/(A+B) − 1/A

⇒ Efficiency of B = Efficiency of (A + B) − Efficiency of A

⇒ Efficiency of B = 4 − 1 = 3 units/day

⇒ Total Work = 56 units

⇒ 3/4 of Total Work = 56 × (3/4) = 42 units

⇒ Time taken by B = 42 ÷ 3 = 14 days

**∴ The correct answer is 14 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Time and Efficiency Relationship

Time taken is inversely proportional to efficiency. Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time.

Combined Work Formula

If two people work together, their combined efficiency is the sum of their individual efficiencies.

Fractional Work

Time for partial work = (Fraction × Total Work) ÷ Efficiency of the person.</p
